key_insight: An oblique-incidence laser vision tracker improves robotic weld seam localization under strong surface reflections, achieving 0.52-pixel extraction accuracy at an average 37 FPS with a 22 mm sensor-to-torch lead distance.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support more reliable robotic arc welding of reflective components in vessels, vehicles and container girders where sensor placement is constrained.
method: Recover laser stripes using a segmentation network with spatial coordinate attention and dual-scale feature fusion.
Reject erroneous stripe inputs using self-iterative random sample consensus.
Integrate seam localization into a robotic weld seam tracker.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on four workpieces with diverse surface conditions and laser-stripe datasets containing large-area noise showed an 81% reduction in seam-position pixel extraction error.
watch_item: Pixel-level results do not establish physical tracking accuracy or weld quality across broader industrial conditions.
paper_title: Study on welding seam tracking for robotic arc welding under strong surface reflection
